title: Local gradient refinement from Round 1 best candidate with ±5% perturbation seed
scientific_hypothesis: The Round 1 best candidate (target_score 0.9531504284001773) resides near a local optimum; sub-nanometer thickness adjustments within ±5% of each layer can further improve the dual-band spectral figure of merit by probing local curvature.
design_principle: Gradient-based local optimization with bounded step size (0.5 nm) to refine thicknesses without escaping the current basin of attraction.
proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers)
design_variables: 30 layer thicknesses initialized from Round 1 best candidate with ±5% multiplicative perturbation
theory_basis: Needle synthesis optimization allows sub-quarter-wave thickness refinement for complex spectral targets
Gradient-based local search can escape shallow local optima with proper step size control
expected_advantages: Tests whether current solution is at true local maximum
known_risks: May converge to same local optimum if basin is flat
Step size limit may slow convergence if curvature is shallow

Evaluate spectral performance across 400-700 nm (target: high reflection) and 1530-1565 nm (target: high transmission). Total layer count fixed at 30. Materials: HfO2 (high index), SiO2 (low index), fused silica substrate. Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 400-700 nm, 1530-1565 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1530–1565 nm; high reflection in 400–700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: reflection in 1530–1565 nm; transmission in 400–700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 30.
